title: Kenya’s Bill of Rights
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Chapter Four. Special groups: children, persons with disabilities, youth, older persons, minorities and marginalised groups. Applying the Bill of Rights: scenario cards.

skills.key_step: The child names rights in Kenya's Bill of Rights, the special groups it protects and how to apply it in daily life.

floor.prerequisite: Names the rights of the child in Kenya.
floor.question: Give one right of the child.

steps: Name a special group and its protection.
contexts: a ramp for a wheelchair user
a learner speaking at a forum

board.do: Write: "A school has no ramp for a learner in a wheelchair."

board.say: Which right and which special group?

board.do: Wait for equality and persons with disabilities.

misconceptions.ask: In which chapter is the Bill of Rights?
misconceptions.repair: Show the chapter list: Chapter 1 is Sovereignty, Chapter 4 the Bill of Rights.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a right in the Bill of Rights?
misconceptions.repair: Read three real rights and ask whether each protects dignity.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a special group protected by the Constitution?
misconceptions.repair: Ask who is more likely to be left out or harmed.

misconceptions.ask: Can the right to free expression be used to spread hate speech?
misconceptions.repair: Read the limit on expression in the Constitution.

checks.question: In which chapter is the Bill of Rights?
Name two special groups protected by the Constitution.
checks.answer: any two of: children, persons with disabilities, youth, older persons, minorities and marginalised groups
